selection.rule: A fix commit enters the corpus when (1) its subject type is fix; (2) its message cites an earlier PR (resolved through the '(#N)' suffix of a squash commit on HEAD) or an earlier commit SHA; (3) git blame at the fix's parent, over the lines the fix removes or changes in .py files, attributes at least one line to the cited commit; (4) the cited commit's diff over reviewable files is at most 110000 characters; (5) it passes the vetting criteria below. The cited commit is the introducer.
selection.reviewable_files: All files in the introducing commit except .md, .mdx, .txt, .json, .jsonl, .lock and anything under .project-toolkit/, .agents/, .serena/, docs/.

criteria: The fix corrects a behavioral defect (wrong result, crash, fail-open, missed case, broken gate, wrong exit code, wrong or non-hermetic test, unwired CI step). Refactors, comment or docstring rewording, feature additions, baseline updates and style cleanups are rejected.
The defect sits in lines the introducing commit added or changed, and the fix message or diff makes that causal link plausible.
A reviewer reading only the introducing diff could in principle see the defect. Defects that needed later knowledge are rejected.
The defect fits in one or two sentences about observable behavior.
vetting.method: Candidates were triaged by Sonnet subagents against these criteria, each reading the fix and introducing commits with git. One reader (Claude) then read all 32 accepted descriptions and checked four against the fix diff. No repository maintainer has reviewed the entries yet.
